about: The data retention review rules. scripts/data_retention_review.py reads this file, so change a unit length, word list, skill need or threshold here and nowhere else. Each key is explained under notes; references/review-checks.md says what each check means.

skill_needs.why: recency bands up to 365+ days, widened to 730 for long purchase cycles
VIP slowdown window up to 365 days
90-day volume baseline for every event type

notes.unit_days: Days in each retention or window unit, as exact fractions. Months and quarters are a twelfth and a quarter of a year, so '12 months' equals '1 year'.
notes.skill_needs: Lookback windows that this repository's skills rely on: each is the event type (or * for every event type) and how many days back the skill reads. An event kept for less is medium, because that skill will under-count.
notes.feeds_live_kinds: Definition kinds that can feed campaigns and scenarios. A window longer than retention in one of these is high; in reports, funnels, trends and dashboards it's medium.
notes.overkeep_factor: An event type kept for more than this many times the longest window anything reads (and at least min_keep_days) is reported as kept longer than it's used.
notes.min_keep_days: The shortest window assumed for any event, so an event nothing reads isn't judged against zero days.
notes.personal_words: Words in a customer or event property name that suggest personal data, by sensitivity. 'high' are special-category or identity-document words; 'medium' direct identifiers and tracking IDs; 'low' indirect ones. Matched against the words of the property name (split on non-letters and camelCase) and each pair of neighbouring words joined (user_agent gives useragent); a word shorter than 4 letters must match exactly, longer words also match as a prefix (birth matches birthdate).
notes.not_personal_words: A property name that contains one of these words is not reported for medium or low words (product_name, campaign_name), only for high ones.
notes.list_limit: At most this many names are quoted in one finding.
notes.max_details: At most this many definitions are fetched by ID in one review (read by the steps in SKILL.md, not the script); the rest are listed as not checked.
